npc_slots_per_screen_state.detail: Hard ceiling 8 NPC entries per (screen, step-state) interact block. RoomEntry7_RoomInit ($0B:$470F) zero-fills exactly $101 bytes at $D7D2 (8 x 32-byte slots + terminator cell $D8D2; FillNBytesWithRegA BC is a plain 16-bit count); the parser (Call_00b_477e) has NO bounds check. Vanilla respects it: valid-step census over all rooms maxes at exactly 8. MEASURED overflow: with 8 entries the terminator lands exactly at $D8D2 (safe); a 9th entry writes into the NPC-script state block — vs an 8-NPC control, corrupts $D8D9 (queued text id) and $D8E2/$D8E3/$D8E6/$D8E7/$D8E8 — silently, no crash. The editor must hard-cap at 8.
npc_slots_per_screen_state.evidence: disassembly/bank_00b.asm RoomEntry7_RoomInit + Call_00b_477e; ROOM_DATA_FORMAT 'NPC capacity & sprite-sheet budget (S91)'

npc_distinct_sprite_sheets_per_screen.detail: NPC sprite sheets load into a shared per-screen VRAM tile budget at room init, first-come in entry order; when the budget is exhausted, later distinct ids render BLANK (no crash, no wedge). Measured: 8 distinct human sheets ($00-$0F range) all render; a batch of 8 distinct boss_composite_fragment ids rendered 2 full + 1 partial + 5 blank. Repeats of the same id are free (share the sheet). Editor meter: warn when adding distinct sprite ids beyond what renders; exact tile counts per sheet are unmeasured (residual).

screens_per_room.detail: Engine scroll math caps at a 4x4 grid = 16 screens (RoomEntry2: row = Y/128 clamped 0-3, col = X/160 clamped 0-3). Vanilla's largest grids are the conveyor/maze rooms mt $54-$59: 12 declared screen slots, 9 with valid steps; screen_index 8 (row 2) render + scroll VERIFIED in PyBoy (warp mt $54 abs (4,18) -> wScreenIndex 8, field renders). S145: CUSTOM rooms take the full 4x4 = 16 too — validators accept screen keys 0-15 ('index outside the 4x4 grid'); the S91 'custom schema 8' was never enforced; measured in the game (tools/walk_fresh_project.py: ATLAS HALL 100 and 150, 4 x 4 each, every screen 0-15 entered in PyBoy, wScreenIndex == k and the picture == the editor preview, in region 0 and region 1). Room dims in the $26DD record must match the screen count (KEY_LESSONS S10 hazard).
screens_per_room.evidence: disassembly/bank_00b.asm RoomEntry2_ScreenScroll; ROOM_DATA_FORMAT 'Scroll Boundary System'; S91 PyBoy warp; PROJECT_COMPILER; S145 tools/walk_fresh_project.py + editor2/tests/test_compiler.py test_s145

screens_per_region.status: structural_s145 + measured_s145; structural_s146 + measured_s146 (screens WITH states only)
screens_per_region.detail: S146 (ROADMAP ARC CAP5): 640 screens WITH STATES per group of 128 rooms. A screen with two or more states (or whose counter label a script names, or with a pinned address) gets a one-byte step counter (Project.step_counter_allocation); every other one-state screen reads ONE shared always-zero byte, wCustomStepZero (the first free address from $CD80) — the original game's rule: 65 single-state screens of its gate / maze / arena rooms point at $D998, which nothing writes. The counters live in the 640-byte area $CD80-$CFFF (custom.wram.region_size, max $280: the wram0 section ends at $D000; PROJECT_COMPILER §2.6) and with regions every region's counters share it (S140; §2.49). The editor (Document.next_free_mapid, S146 (b)) puts a new room into the next region once a region's counters are 90 % used (project.STEP_GROUP_FULL; project.counter_use). Measured S146 (tools/walk_counters.py): 128 rooms x 6 one-state screens (768 screens, which stopped the S145 build) use 1 byte; 100 rooms x 6 two-state screens fill region 1 to 577 bytes and the last 4 go to region 2 — built and walked in PyBoy on the user's save, 1,988 checks, 0 failed. S145 (historical): every screen took a byte, one-state screens too — 128 rooms x 6 screens stopped the build.

custom_mapids.detail: wMapID is one byte. Until S137 bank $17 CustomAttrCheck (+ its two callers label17_401d / label17_409e) indexed per-room tables with `sub $6B / add a / add l` — an 8-bit doubling that drops the carry, so $EB+ silently read another room's data; bank $60's readers index [wPlaceIdx] since S136 and bank $17 reads a one-room WRAM table since S137, but PlaceDirectory is filled for $6B-$EA only and bank $71's per-room tables are sized for the project's rooms (S138: every reader bounded — a custom id with no place reads the Castle record and is sent home at CONTINUE, tools/census_stale_places.py). editor2/core/project.py CUSTOM_MID_MAX = $EA (ProjectError past it, test_compiler test_s133). Room-default / battle music tables: 256 rows since S138 (every custom id; they stopped at $7F S64-S137). Hard id max $FE ($FF = list terminator / skill script type). Lifting it = ROADMAP ARC CAP (regions: the id range per region). S140 (ARC CAP3a, USER-CONFIRMED 2026-10-10): a place = (wMapRegion, wMapID); every per-place table (banks $60 / $6C / $71 / $76) is indexed by a 16-bit place number (PlaceNum<bank>, templates/place_number.asm); $EB-$FE = exit link ids; the arena copies are region-0 global places; compiler REGION_MAX 63; bank $71's tables cost 15 B a place (8 record + 3 encounters + 1 anim + 1 flags + 2 songs) -> ~950 places with ~2 KB of fixed code / rows. Measured: census_regions 337 places in 4 regions, 0 mismatched; PyBoy: map id $76 in four regions on the user's save. S145: the per-place cost in the banks that do not spill measured on fresh projects (blank template + 20 / 40 rooms): bank $71 +15 B a place, bank $76 +3 B (test_compiler.test_s145) — bank $71's free bytes / 15 is the room ceiling the Capacity tab shows (≈950 for a project with few other bank-$71 rows; 959 for the S145 160-room acceptance project).

rom_size.value: 4 MB (256 banks, MBC5 8-bit ROMB0) — BUILT S134: every patched build; banks $80-$FF self-ID stubs until the compiler fills them (S135: the LZ stream overflow banks; ARC CAP2b: place banks); USER-CONFIRMED S135
rom_size.detail: Scratch build with SECTIONs in banks $80 / $FF: rgblink links, rgbfix -p pads to 4 MB and sets $0148 = $07; PyBoy boots it to the bedroom and maps banks $80 / $FF through $2100. No engine code tests bit 7 of a bank number; the 23 ROMB0 writes are all ROM0, full 8 bits; nothing writes ROMB1. Requirement: every new bank starts with its own number (db <bank> at $4000) — AudioSaveBankState / rst $10 / the text engine save the current bank by reading [$4000]. A real rst $10 into bank $80 RAN in PyBoy (scratch probe: bank $73 CF2WarpCommitDrain far-called a bank $80 entry on every commit — 3 warps, 3 calls, the callee read $80 at [$4000], every room loaded and walked). 8 MB (ROMB1) would need 9-bit bank numbers through every far call — not planned.
